title: post-incident-reservation-rightsizing-and-granular-burst-controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A dedicated cluster capacity incident on 2026-02-22 revealed two compounding issues: (1) a reservation-sizing mismatch where several production reservations were under-provisioned relative to their observed steady-state working set, and (2) an overly permissive burst policy that allowed tenants to consume short-term tokens that triggered cache pressure and downstream eviction cascades. Result: elevated tail latency for critical routes, tokenized failures in the routing layer, and multiple customer retries that increased cost. Root cause analysis identified gaps in reservation telemetry, no per-reservation burst budgeting at the scheduler, and unclear runbook guidance for emergency reservation adjustments. This ticket captures a prioritized set of mitigations, instrumentation changes, and operational guardrails to reduce recurrence and give operators safer controls for controlled capacity changes.
action_items: Rightsize reservations: develop an automated suggestion engine that recommends reservation sizes based on 30/90/180-day token and concurrency distributions. Owner: Miguel Torres. ETA: 2026-03-24.
Per-reservation burst limiter: implement a leaky-bucket burst token system at the scheduler level with configurable refill rate and max-burst. Owner: Runtime Team (Leah Nguyen). ETA: 2026-04-07.

Eviction pacing controller: introduce a pacing mechanism to limit concurrent evictions per-node to avoid cascading pressure across LRU/KV caches. Owner: Systems Reliability (Rahul Iyer). ETA: 2026-03-31.

Reservation headroom dashboard: add a dashboard with headroom % (reservation vs 95th percentile usage), projected 24h exhaustion time, and alert thresholds. Owner: Observability (Sofia Martinez). ETA: 2026-03-17.

Canary strategy for reservation changes: create an automated canary rollout for reservation bumps (10% of pods -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback on latency/eviction signals. Owner: Platform (Miguel Torres). ETA: 2026-04-10.

Runbook update & emergency recipe: publish a concise emergency ops recipe for 'soft reservation bump' vs 'hard reallocation' including safe rollback steps and post-action validation checks. Owner: On-call Lead (Priya Shah). ETA: 2026-03-12.

Cost model delta check: extend the billing estimator to surface expected monthly cost delta for candidate reservation changes and burst policy updates. Owner: Finance Eng (Ben Carlson). ETA: 2026-04-01.

Add per-tenant noisy-neighbor signals: emit a "burst-score" and cache-pressure metric per tenant that feeds routing decisions and can trigger temporary throttling. Owner: Runtime + Dataplane (Leah Nguyen, Rahul Iyer). ETA: 2026-03-28.
acceptance_criteria: Automated reservation suggestions deployed to staging with validation against historical traces and a false-positive rate < 10%.
Burst limiter in staging that prevents short-term token spikes from causing >20% increase in node eviction rate.
Eviction pacing reduces simultaneous eviction activities per-node to <= 3 by default and is configurable.
Headroom dashboard shows correct 95th usage and sends alerts when projected exhaustion < 12 hours.
Canary reservation rollout executed successfully on a production-like canary with no customer-visible errors and documented rollback path.
Runbook published in Confluence and linked in on-call Slack with a quick reference card.
Metric "burst-score" appears in telemetry and is used in at least one routing fallback rule in staging.
updates: 2026-02-24 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident summary call; linked initial tracing artifacts and high-level RCA notes.
2026-02-27 - Miguel Torres: Collected 90-day token histograms and identified three reservations that were consistently >110% of their committed reservation during peak hours.
2026-03-03 - Leah Nguyen: Spike reproduction in staging shows short bursts with >2x CPU and KV pressure; prototype leaky-bucket limiter reduced cache churn by 35%.
2026-03-07 - Observability: Dashboard wireframe reviewed; added projected exhaustion and per-reservation 95th percentile lines. Feedback: include predicted cost delta for each suggested resize.
2026-03-10 - Priya Shah: Drafted emergency runbook and tested 'soft bump' sequence on the non-customer-facing cluster; results logged and safe rollback validated.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates short-term operator controls (runbook + soft bump) from medium-term engineering fixes (burst limiter, reservation suggestion engine). We should avoid large emergency reservation patches that lack canary safety. Coordinate with sales/success for any impacted customer comms if canaries detect instability.
